turns.t: Sorry, we're a bit early. This is Poppy, and Jade here looks after her in the daytime. ~
Not at all, come in. Hello Poppy! Jade, hello. Who wants to tell me how we're getting on since the ear? ~
I can start, I've had her four days this week. She's much happier, aren't you, poppet? ~
Ear better. ~
That's what I like to hear. Mum, remind me what happened last week? ~
She was tugging at her ear and screaming half the night, Tuesday and Wednesday. Then she gave her the pink stuff. Oh, what's it called.
Amoxicillin, it's on the bottle. 250 mg, three times a day. We're on the last two days of it.
That's it. I give the morning and teatime ones, and Jade does lunch.
Brilliant. And is the tugging still happening?
No, that's gone completely. She hasn't touched it since Friday, I think. It's gone now.
Good. Any fever since you started it?
No fever, not since the first night.
Any fluid or gunk coming out of the ear?
No, nothing. I check her pillow every nap, there's never anything on it.
Lovely. Does she have anything for pain, or has she needed anything?
Just ibuprofen, 5 ml at bedtime, if she's grizzly. She hasn't needed it for two days.
Good. Is she allergic to anything? Any allergies to medicines or foods?
No, none. She's eaten everything and been fine on the amoxicillin.
Wonderful. And remind me of her health background?
She has eczema, mostly on her elbows. And she's had a few ear infections, this is the third.
Right. Poppy, shall I have a look in your ears? It's like a little torch. ~
Torch! ~
Ooh, you're brilliant. Hold really still, that's it.
Is she being good? ~
She's being perfect. Her temperature is 36.8 and she weighs 14.2 kilos.
Was she heavier last time? ~
Not that I can see, she's right on track. Now, the right eardrum looks normal. Pink and shiny, no redness.
And the left? ~
The left is the one that was infected, and it's looking much calmer. I think the ear infection has settled.
Oh, thank goodness. So she's all done? ~
Nearly. Finish the last two days of the amoxicillin, then stop. It's worth checking how she hears after a few infections, so I'd like to arrange a hearing check.
Does that hurt her? ~
Not at all, it's a game with headphones and beeps. ~
And when would that be? ~
The appointment will come by post. And I'd like to see her again in six weeks, so we can check the ear and talk about the hearing test.
Six weeks, I'll put it in the calendar. ~
Bring her back sooner if she's pulling at it again or has a temperature.
We will. Say bye-bye, Poppy. ~
Bye, doctor! ~
